oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: se-alert-high - multiple 5xx from API gateway in eu-west1, possible deploy/migration issue. Ran runbook checks, creating thread for on-call. thread_ts=2460100000

maria (sre): seeing spike in 500s on /profiles/update and some background job failures. % of requests small (~2.3% globally) but concentrated in eu-west1. First noticed at ~23:26 UTC.

ken (frontend): confirmed canary rollout 2026.03.10 reached 3/10 canaries in eu-west1 around 23:20. No frontend code referencing new columns AFAIK, but frontend toggles a feature flag for new profile flow.

anya (backend): rollback flag tripped in canary-svc logs: "ERROR: insert into profiles failed: column \"preferred_name\" does not exist". That sounds like schema mismatch between app and DB.

liam (db): I see a migration started as part of release 20260310_add_preferred_name (migration id: 20260310_add_preferred_name). It partially applied — the DDL to add column on primary node completed, but a replica lag / replica failover prevented schema propagation to read replicas used by some pods. Also background backfill job failed with constraint errors.

maria (sre): ok immediate mitigation: stop rollout, pause autoscaler, and flip feature flag that writes to new column to off. Can someone flip the flag? @zach can you kill-write-ff:profile_write_new?

zach (pm): doing it now: /ff toggle profile_write_new off --env prod --region eu-west1

deploy-bot: Command received: /ff toggle profile_write_new off --env prod --region eu-west1. Toggled flag -> OFF.

anya (backend): thanks. I'm seeing writes attempting new column still from a few pods pinned to older DB reader endpoints. I'll temporarily adjust app traffic by draining canary instances.

maria (sre): kubectl scale deployment/canary-profiles -n prod --replicas=0 for the 3 failing canaries.

ken (frontend): done scaling canary-profiles to 0 in eu-west1. Rolling back canary release?

maria (sre): yes, run rollback on the service (don't touch DB migrations yet).

deploy-bot: Triggering rollback: /deploy rollback canary-profiles to v2026.03.09. Rollback started.

liam (db): I'm investigating DB state. Running psql on primary: 

```
-- psql
SELECT column_name, is_nullable, data_type
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name='profiles' AND column_name='preferred_name';
```

Result: column exists on primary: preferred_name text NULL. But read-replica nodes show no such column. Replica lag of ~45s and one replica failed replication due to transient auth error earlier.

liam (db): cause of 500s is read queries routed to a replica missing the column returning error, app treated as 500. Writes to primary succeeded but backfill tasks that read from replicas failed.

anya (backend): so partial DDL + eventual read routing caused runtime error. For safety we should put a temporary middleware to treat missing-column errors as gracefully degraded instead of 500, but that's risky. Let's keep current mitigation: feature-flag off + rollback.

maria (sre): Next steps: get replicas healthy, ensure schema present on all replicas, then run backfill + add NOT NULL if needed. Liam, can you promote/repair replica or re-sync? ETA?

liam (db): I'm re-initializing the failed replica (rebuild from snapshot), ETA ~12-20 min, replication should catch up then. After replicas healthy, we should run a safe DDL path: (1) add column NULL, (2) backfill in batches, (3) set NOT NULL with validation. Also add traffic-safe guardrails (app feature flag only enables write after backfill complete).

sophie (support): any customer impact notes I should pass along? We have two enterprise customers in eu-west1 seeing profile update failures intermittently. No data loss reported.

maria (sre): severity: S3 (partial impact) for a subset of customers in eu-west1. Notify CS to update impacted customers: describe symptom as intermittent profile update failures, we rolled back the canary and disabled the new profile writes, fix in progress.

zach (pm): I'll draft a short customer message.

maria (sre): Handoff: I'm on-call for 6 more hours. If replica rebuild completes and DDL plan ready, we'll coordinate a safe re-release. If anything changes escalate to pager.

liam (db): Replica rebuild started. Running check: `SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();` and `pg_stat_replication` to monitor lag. Will post updates.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed for canary-profiles to v2026.03.09. All canaries scaled down.

anya (backend): after rollback, error rate on /profiles/update dropped to baseline ~5m after. No new 500 spikes.

maria (sre): Good. Action items assigned: 
- liam (db): complete replica rebuild + confirm schema sync (target +20m)
- anya (backend): prepare migration-safe playbook, and a toggle that only enables writes after explicit backfill flag
- ken (frontend): ensure client toggles don't write to new column until backend confirms
- zach (pm)/sophie (support): customer comms drafted and sent to impacted accounts

liam (db): replica back to healthy; `pg_stat_replication` shows lag <1s. Running schema sync check across readers: all readers now report `preferred_name` present.

maria (sre): good. Anya, can you run backfill in small batches now? Please include monitoring and an abort plan.

anya (backend): starting backfill job (id: bf-20260310-profiles) with batch_size=5000, dry-run mode first. I'll post logs.

anya (backend): dry-run ok. Starting real backfill.

maria (sre): monitoring tokens: watch error rate and 5xx, CPU, and replication lag. If any regression, immediate stop and escalate.

anya (backend): backfill completed ~25m. Verified row counts. Running validation: sampling reads across replicas and primary OK. Will schedule a short deploy window to re-enable feature flag and lightweight canary (0.5% traffic) after deploy-team signoff.

maria (sre): schedule: re-release window 01:05 UTC with explicit pre-checks. If green, enable ff (profile_write_new) in staged rollout: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> full.

zach (pm): customer note sent: "We've paused a recent profile rollout after a partial database schema application led to intermittent failures for some customers in EU. We rolled back the canary and disabled the profile write flag. Our engineers rebuilt the replica, completed a safe backfill, and will re-run the rollout in a controlled staged manner. No data loss reported; we will follow up when rollout completes."

sophie (support): customers acknowledged, will keep watch.

maria (sre): closing thread for now. If anything flares up re-ping oncall. Thanks all for fast coordination. :heart:
